specification:
---
feature: web-calculator
change_kind: feature
---

## Summary

A browser-based calculator supporting basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction,
multiplication, division, decimals), keyboard input, clear/backspace
functions, and user-selectable light/dark themes that persist across browser
sessions. The interface is responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile
viewports and requires no installation or authentication.

Open items not decided by this specification: the PRD does not mandate a
technology stack or file layout, so the declared artifacts below reflect one
plausible static HTML/CSS/JS structure rather than a design mandate; this
should be confirmed rather than assumed. The PRD also does not define
behavior for error conditions such as division by zero or malformed input
sequences, so no acceptance criteria are written for those cases. RQ-012
requires keyboard support for numbers, operators, Enter, Backspace, and
Escape without specifying the exact behavior each key triggers: the specific
keyboard-to-operator key bindings in AC-013, the mapping of Enter to the
equals action in AC-014, and the mapping of Escape to the clear action in
AC-016 are all interpretations of RQ-012's generic wording rather than
explicit PRD statements, and are disclosed here on equal footing rather than
singled out.

## Declared artifacts

- index.html
- css/styles.css
- js/calculator.js
- js/theme.js

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: The application loads and runs entirely within a modern web browser with no installation step.
- AC-002: The calculator displays number buttons for digits 0 through 9, each of which appends the corresponding digit to the current entry.
- AC-003: Selecting the addition (+) button applies addition between the current operands.
- AC-004: Selecting the subtraction (-) button applies subtraction between the current operands.
- AC-005: Selecting the multiplication (×) button applies multiplication between the current operands.
- AC-006: Selecting the division (÷) button applies division between the current operands.
- AC-007: The application accepts decimal point input and correctly evaluates expressions containing decimal values.
- AC-008: Entered values and calculation results are shown in a visible display area at all times during interaction.
- AC-009: Selecting the clear (C) button resets the current entry, operator, and pending operand to an initial empty state.
- AC-010: Selecting the backspace/delete control removes only the most recently entered character from the current entry without affecting prior operands.
- AC-011: Selecting the equals (=) button computes and displays the result of the current expression.
- AC-012: Pressing number keys (0-9) on the keyboard enters the corresponding digit into the display.
- AC-013: Pressing operator keys (+, -, *, /) on the keyboard applies the corresponding arithmetic operation.
- AC-014: Pressing Enter on the keyboard triggers the same result calculation as selecting the equals button.
- AC-015: Pressing Backspace on the keyboard removes the most recently entered character.
- AC-016: Pressing Escape on the keyboard clears the current calculation, equivalent to selecting the clear (C) button.
- AC-017: The application provides a control to toggle between Light Mode and Dark Mode, and the active theme is visually reflected in the interface.
- AC-018: The user's selected theme is restored automatically when the application is reloaded or reopened in a new browser session.
- AC-019: The calculator layout renders correctly and remains fully usable at viewport widths from 320 pixels up through desktop screen sizes.
- AC-020: Interactive buttons display a visibly distinct hover state and a visibly distinct focus state, and text maintains sufficient contrast in both the light and dark themes.
- AC-021: The application loads and becomes interactive within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
- AC-022: The application does not require user authentication or account creation to access or use any calculator function.

## Tasks

Create index.html with the calculator markup: display area, digit buttons 0-9, decimal point button, operator buttons (+, -, x, /), equals button, clear (C) button, backspace button, and a theme toggle control
Link css/styles.css and js/calculator.js and js/theme.js from index.html
Implement css/styles.css with a responsive grid/flex layout for the calculator that renders correctly from 320px viewport width up through desktop sizes
Define light and dark theme styles in css/styles.css using CSS custom properties or a theme class toggled on a root element, ensuring sufficient text contrast in both themes
Add visibly distinct hover and focus states for all interactive buttons in css/styles.css
Implement js/calculator.js to track current entry, pending operand, and selected operator in state, updating the display on every input
Wire digit button clicks (0-9) to append digits to the current entry and update the display
Wire decimal point input to add a decimal point to the current entry, guarding against multiple decimal points in a single number
Wire operator button clicks (+, -, x, /) to store the pending operand and operator, applying the arithmetic operation when the next value is entered or equals is pressed
Wire the equals button to compute and display the result of the current expression
Wire the clear (C) button to reset current entry, operator, and pending operand to an initial empty state
Wire the backspace/delete control to remove only the most recently entered character from the current entry
Add a keydown listener in js/calculator.js mapping number keys 0-9 to digit entry, operator keys (+, -, *, /) to the corresponding operations, Enter to the equals action, Backspace to the backspace action, and Escape to the clear action
Implement js/theme.js to toggle a light/dark theme class or attribute on the document root when the theme control is activated, updating the toggle control's visual state to reflect the active theme
Persist the selected theme in localStorage in js/theme.js and restore it on page load before first paint to avoid a flash of the wrong theme
Manually verify the calculator loads and is usable in a browser with no build/install step and no authentication prompt
Manually verify load-and-interactive time is within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection using browser devtools performance/network timing
